rules.name: Modus ponens
preconditions: Both premises are established in the same proof context
rules.operation: Infer the consequent from an established antecedent and implication.
examples: If x is even implies x^2 is even and x is even, then infer x^2 is even
counterexamples: From Q and P implies Q, inferring P is invalid

rules.name: Modus tollens
rules.input_form: P implies Q and not Q
preconditions: Both premises are established in the same proof context
rules.operation: Reject an antecedent whose implication has a false consequent.
examples: If P implies Q but Q is false, then P cannot hold
counterexamples: From not P and P implies Q, inferring not Q is invalid

rules.name: Proof by cases pattern
rules.input_form: P or Q, plus R from P and R from Q
preconditions: All case conclusions derive the same target statement
rules.operation: Infer a common result after exhausting the declared cases.
examples: Parity arguments often split into even and odd cases and conclude the same target statement
counterexamples: Concluding R when only one case has been handled is invalid

rules.name: Universal instantiation
preconditions: a is a valid term in the declared domain
rules.operation: Instantiate a universally quantified formula at a valid term.
examples: From forall x in R, x^2 >= 0, infer a^2 >= 0 for a in R
counterexamples: Instantiating with a term outside the declared domain is invalid

rules.name: Existential witness introduction
preconditions: a is a valid witness term
rules.operation: Introduce an existential statement from a witnessed instance.
examples: From 2 is prime, infer there exists a prime number
counterexamples: Asserting a universal statement from one witness is invalid

rules.name: Equality substitution rule
rules.input_form: a = b and a well-formed context containing a
rules.output_form: same context with a replaced by b
preconditions: Replacement preserves well-formedness
rules.operation: Substitute equals for equals in a well-formed logical or mathematical context.
examples: From a = b and f(a) = 0, infer f(b) = 0
counterexamples: Substituting into only part of a structured occurrence inconsistently is invalid

rules.name: Set extensionality
rules.input_form: forall x, x in A iff x in B
preconditions: Membership equivalence is established for arbitrary x
rules.operation: Conclude set equality from equality of membership conditions.
examples: If every x belongs to A exactly when x belongs to B, then A = B
counterexamples: Sharing some elements is insufficient for set equality

rules.name: Contradiction rule
preconditions: An explicit contradiction is derived in classical logic
rules.operation: Discharge an assumption once it leads to contradiction.
examples: Indirect proofs discharge a negated goal after deriving contradiction
counterexamples: Declaring contradiction without an explicit incompatible pair of statements is invalid

rules.name: Induction schema
rules.output_form: statement for all naturals in range
preconditions: The base case and successor implication are both valid
rules.operation: Extend a proposition across the natural numbers by induction.
examples: Induction proves sum identities over N
counterexamples: Omitting the base case or the successor implication invalidates the schema

rules.name: Negated universal equivalence
rules.output_form: exists x such that not P(x)
preconditions: Quantifiers range over the same declared domain
rules.operation: Push negation across a universal quantifier by converting it to an existential quantifier.
examples: If not every real number is positive, then some real number is not positive
counterexamples: Replacing not forall x, P(x) by forall x, not P(x) is invalid in general

rules.name: Negated existential equivalence
rules.input_form: not exists x such that P(x)
preconditions: Quantifiers range over the same declared domain
rules.operation: Push negation across an existential quantifier by converting it to a universal quantifier.
examples: If no integer in a set is odd, then every integer in the set is not odd
counterexamples: Replacing not exists x, P(x) by exists x, not P(x) is invalid in general

rules.name: Alpha-renaming of bound variables
rules.output_form: equivalent formula with a fresh bound variable name
preconditions: Variable capture is avoided during renaming
rules.operation: Rename a bound variable without changing the semantic content of the formula.
examples: forall x, P(x) is equivalent to forall y, P(y) when y is fresh in the formula
counterexamples: Renaming a bound variable to one already free in the scope can change meaning and is invalid

rules.name: Implication elimination rewrite
rules.operation: Rewrite implication into disjunction to normalize formulas.
examples: Implication elimination reduces formulas toward disjunctive and conjunctive normal-form pipelines
counterexamples: Rewriting P implies Q as P or Q is invalid

rules.name: De Morgan rewrite for conjunction and disjunction
rules.output_form: equivalent formula with negation pushed inward
rules.operation: Apply De Morgan's laws to move negation inward through conjunction or disjunction.
examples: Pushing negations inward is a standard normalization step
counterexamples: Dropping negations on both operands during rewriting is invalid

rules.name: CNF distribution seed rule
rules.operation: Distribute disjunction over conjunction as a seed step toward conjunctive normal form.
examples: Distributing disjunction over conjunction moves a formula toward conjunctive normal form
counterexamples: Distributing in the wrong direction can change the formula and is invalid

rules.name: Deduction theorem pattern
rules.input_form: derivation of Q from Gamma together with P
rules.output_form: derivation of P implies Q from Gamma
preconditions: The active proof calculus satisfies the standard deduction-theorem hypotheses
rules.operation: Convert a derivation under a temporary assumption into a conditional conclusion.
examples: Proving a conditional may proceed by temporarily assuming the antecedent and deriving the consequent
counterexamples: Using the deduction theorem in a proof system where its side conditions fail is invalid

rules.name: Soundness seed
rules.input_form: provable statement in the active proof system
rules.output_form: semantic validity in the intended models
preconditions: A semantics has been specified for the proof system
rules.operation: Connect derivability to semantic validity through a soundness principle.
examples: Soundness prevents the derivation system from proving false statements in all models
counterexamples: Claiming derivability of semantically invalid formulas under a sound system is invalid

rules.name: Completeness seed
rules.output_form: derivable statement in a complete proof system
preconditions: A complete proof system is under discussion
rules.operation: Connect semantic validity back to derivability through a completeness principle.
examples: Completeness connects model-theoretic validity back to derivability
counterexamples: Treating non-derivability in an incomplete fragment as disproof of semantic validity is invalid

rules.name: Set-builder membership expansion
rules.input_form: x in {y in A such that P(y)}
preconditions: The ambient set A and predicate P are well-formed
rules.operation: Expand set-builder membership into ambient-set membership and predicate satisfaction.
examples: Membership in a filtered set splits into ambient membership plus predicate satisfaction
counterexamples: Treating predicate satisfaction alone as enough for membership without ambient-set membership is invalid

rules.name: Subset criterion
rules.output_form: forall x, x in A implies x in B
rules.operation: Reduce a subset claim to a universal membership implication.
examples: Proving subset relations reduces to a universally quantified membership implication
counterexamples: Checking only some sample elements does not prove a subset relation

rules.name: Union and intersection membership laws
rules.input_form: x in A union B or x in A intersection B
rules.operation: Rewrite union and intersection membership into propositional membership formulas.
examples: Elementwise set identities reduce to propositional membership formulas
counterexamples: Using and in place of or for union membership is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Composition rule expansion
rules.input_form: objects A and B with a valid composition law
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Compose structured objects when composition preconditions are satisfied.
examples: Function and operator compositions require compatible codomain-domain interfaces
counterexamples: Composing incompatible objects is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Inverse admissibility expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Introduce inverses only when invertibility conditions are explicitly satisfied.
examples: Matrix inversion requires nonsingularity
counterexamples: Assuming inverses exist without conditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions
